item.title: Why Some Players Prefer CroreWin Over Bigger Betting Platforms
item.description: Bigger doesn’t always mean better. That’s something more players are starting to realize, especially after spending time on the usual large-name platforms.

item.title: Trump delays strikes on Iran's energy grid by five days, claims “productive” talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced on Monday a five-day moratorium on the threatened attacks against Iran's energy infrastructure, hours before the 48-hour ultimatum he issued on Saturday demanding Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz was set to expire.

item.title: Milei willing to send troops to the Middle East if requested by Trump
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei's willingness to send troops to the Middle East if requested by the United States has fuelled growing concern in Argentina, a country that has historically maintained an equidistant stance on international conflicts and where fears of possible reprisals are emerging.

item.title: “I messed up”: harrowing ATC audio emerges after fatal LaGuardia crash
item.description: “We were dealing with an emergency earlier and I messed up.” The air traffic controller's voice at New York's LaGuardia Airport sounds shaken in tower frequency recordings released through LiveATC.net, barely twenty minutes after an Air Canada plane collided with a fire truck on the runway, killing the pilot and copilot.

item.title: Dollar falls and São Paulo stock exchange surges after Trump's truce signal with Iran
item.description: Brazilian financial markets posted one of their best sessions of the year on Monday after President Donald Trump announced a five-day postponement of strikes against Iran's energy infrastructure, citing “productive conversations” with Tehran.

item.title: Colombian military plane crashes after takeoff with more than 120 people on board
item.description: A Colombian Air Force C-130 Hercules crashed on Monday shortly after taking off from La Tagua airstrip in Puerto Leguízamo, Putumayo, in southern Colombia, with at least 125 people on board. The aircraft was heading to Puerto Asís, also in Putumayo, carrying troops on a routine rotation.

item.title: Analysts warn $200 oil is no longer a far-fetched scenario
item.description: Oil prices could surpass $150 per barrel and approach $200 if the Strait of Hormuz blockade persists, according to energy industry analysts — a level that would make a global recession virtually inevitable.

item.title: Argentina marches on 50th anniversary of coup that led to the Falklands War and the regime's fall
item.description: Thousands of people are expected to gather this Tuesday in Plaza de Mayo and in Argentina’s major cities to mark the 50th anniversary of the March 24, 1976, military coup that installed a dictatorship responsible for thousands of forced disappearances and which, in its final stage, launched the Falklands War in a desperate bid to cling to power.

item.title: Chile withdraws support for Bachelet's candidacy for UN Secretary General
item.description: The government of José Antonio Kast on Tuesday withdrew Chile's backing for former President Michelle Bachelet's bid to lead the United Nations, deeming her candidacy “unviable” in the current context.

item.title: USS Nimitz to operate in Uruguayan waters on final deployment before decommissioning
item.description: The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Nimitz (CVN-68), flagship of the United States Navy for more than five decades, will arrive in Uruguayan waters in the coming weeks as part of the “Southern Seas 2026” deployment, the US Fourth Fleet announced.
